finding.result: The pinned Cargo local-registry implementation explicitly models a registry as on-disk .crate files plus an index directory. Its update path performs no remote update and only verifies that the registry root and index directories exist. config() returns None because local registries have no remote API configuration, invalidate_cache() states there is no cache and reads from disk, is_updated() returns true because there is nothing to update, and download() opens the local .crate tarball and verifies its checksum; the source comments state it does not actually download anything, while finish_download() panics because this source does not download.
finding.phase1_relevance: This is exact positive mechanism evidence that Cargo has a filesystem-backed registry source whose package/index reads and tarball acquisition path do not require a remote registry API or network download once the local registry is already populated. It does not prove scheduled Chat can populate that registry, invoke Cargo, or complete dependency resolution end-to-end.
finding.verified_scope: Exactly one read-only official rust-lang/cargo blob lookup for blob 1b244c07924b69270046322face63214e4506691, limited to explicit behavior in that pinned local-registry implementation.
finding.not_verified_scope: How source replacement selects local-registry, how the registry is populated, dependency resolution outside this implementation, Cargo process execution from scheduled Chat, filesystem persistence availability, arbitrary Cargo versions, and end-to-end Chat parity remain untested.

scope_guard: Do not infer end-to-end offline Cargo operation or Chat-native execution from this file. The positive claim is limited to the pinned implementation's local filesystem registry behavior after required files already exist.

hard_gate_assessment.positive_evidence_scope: Pinned Cargo LocalRegistry on-disk read/checksum/no-remote-download behavior only; no end-to-end parity claim.
